H6LA05291.name: Dan McKay
H6LA05291.bio: Lawyer with a country law practice in Avoyelles Parish for over 45 years and U.S. Army veteran.

positions.stance: Says democratic principles are under attack; supports separation of church and state, free and fair elections, rule of law, and a free press.
Views health care as a human right and opposes Medicaid cuts he says threaten about 20 rural hospitals in the district.
Concerned about rural population loss, blight, and data centers straining water systems; says repeated tax cuts favor only the wealthiest.
Opposes government and business compiling extensive dossiers on Americans and says privacy must be given priority.
Supports international alliances including NATO, which he says is being weakened.

H6KY01110.name: James R. Comer
H6KY01110.bio: U.S. Representative, chairman of the House Oversight Committee, and former Kentucky Commissioner of Agriculture.

positions.stance: Has spent his life advocating for Kentucky's farmers and rural producers.
Supports continued federal funding for Kentucky schools while keeping federal education policy focused on students rather than Washington bureaucrats.
Supports protecting rural healthcare providers, strengthening Medicare, and giving patients greater control over their healthcare decisions.
Committed to a strong national defense, military readiness, servicemembers' quality of life, and ensuring Fort Campbell has needed resources.
Says the Oversight Committee under his leadership has investigated waste, fraud, abuse, and mismanagement across the federal government.
Opposes a methane tax and changes to stepped-up basis and capital gains taxes that could force families to sell their farms.
Supports a balanced budget amendment and says Congress must balance the budget and address the growing national debt.
Fights for resources to support Fort Knox military families and improve the military's readiness.
Advances policies meant to lower health care costs by increasing competition and price transparency.
Supports apprenticeships and work-based learning, pushes back on burdensome regulations, and backs stronger U.S. supply chains less dependent on China.

H0KY05015.name: Hal Rogers
H0KY05015.bio: U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 5th District and former chairman of the House Appropriations Committee.

positions.stance: Says that as Appropriations chairman he pursued discretionary spending cuts, rigorous oversight, and an open, transparent process.
Supports projects promoting economic development, job creation, stronger infrastructure, and a better standard of living in Kentucky's 5th District.
Aims to give southern and eastern Kentucky students educational and career training opportunities so they can build their futures in the region.
Advocates for domestic energy production, particularly safe and environmentally responsible coal mining, and keeping energy and gas prices low.
Co-founded the PRIDE program to preserve the region's natural beauty, including sanitary sewers, trash-free roads, and clean lakes and streams.

H8IA02043.name: Mariannette Miller-Meeks
H8IA02043.bio: U.S. Representative, physician, and veteran who formerly directed the Iowa Department of Public Health.

positions.stance: Says she has worked to cut taxes, secure the border, strengthen the military, and lower health care costs.
Says Biden-era policies drove up inflation and household costs and amounted to a war on American energy.
Believes every American child deserves access to a quality education.
Led efforts to ensure fracking cannot be banned, saying it produces affordable energy and strengthens national security.
Says she has worked in Congress to lower drug prices so people receive care at an affordable cost.

H8NV03036.name: Dina Titus
H8NV03036.bio: U.S. Representative for Nevada's 1st District and senior member of the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.

positions.stance: Champions workers' rights to unionize and bargain collectively, and supports raising the minimum wage to $15 per hour.
Fights for animal welfare, including ending inhumane animal experiments by government agencies and defending wild horses and burros.
Believes diplomacy must be the foundation of U.S. foreign policy, with the U.S. standing with allies on global challenges.
Supports reforming the immigration system with a pathway to citizenship for law-abiding immigrants and protections for DREAMers and TPS holders.
Introduced legislation banning bump stocks and co-sponsored bills to ban assault weapons and require comprehensive background checks.

H0AR03055.name: Steve Womack
H0AR03055.bio: U.S. Representative for Arkansas's 3rd District and 30-year veteran of the Army National Guard.

positions.stance: Believes life begins at conception and opposes any use of taxpayer funds for abortion.
Pledges to work with Arkansas's congressional delegation to ensure the state's farmers are represented in Washington.
Will fight for pro-growth policies that benefit Arkansans, protect American jobs, and ensure continued prosperity.
Committed to cutting spending; has voted for a balanced budget amendment and works to reduce discretionary spending.
Will work to ensure the military has what it needs to keep the nation safe and protect its way of life.

H6MS01131.name: Trent Kelly
H6MS01131.bio: U.S. Representative for Mississippi's 1st District who served 39 years in the Mississippi National Guard.

positions.stance: Believes the federal government's primary role is keeping the U.S. safe, and that responsibility to veterans continues after their service.
Will fight to defend the Second Amendment rights of law-abiding gun owners.
Will pursue policies on the Agriculture Committee that encourage rural development and help agriculture innovate and succeed.
Says Washington rules and regulations increase costs, hinder job growth, and stifle investment.
Supports an all-of-the-above energy strategy and says the federal government should not pick winners and losers.

H4MT02098.name: Troy Downing
H4MT02098.bio: U.S. Representative for Montana's 2nd District and U.S. Air Force veteran.

positions.stance: Strongly supports making the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act permanent and expanding access to capital for rural small businesses.
Says education should be handled by state and local communities and supports reducing federal overreach in education.
Supports an all-of-the-above energy approach, calls fossil fuels abundant and cost-efficient, and backs Montana coal mining.
Supports health care policies that empower individuals, lower costs by promoting competition, and protect access to telemedicine.
Says veterans need high-quality health benefits and better mental health care, and has cosponsored bills to support them.

H4RI01265.name: Gabe Amo
H4RI01265.bio: U.S. Representative for Rhode Island's 1st District and former deputy director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs.

positions.stance: Prioritizes strengthening retirement security for seniors.
Prioritizes ending gun violence.
Prioritizes ensuring resilience to climate change.
Prioritizes securing reproductive freedom.
Prioritizes protecting democracy.
